ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, we have $AB=AC$, and $BD$ bisects $\angle ABC$ and intersects $AC$ at point $D$. Point $E$ is on the extension line of $BC$, and $BD=DE$. Point $G$ is the midpoint of the line segment $BC$. We draw line $AG$ and it intersects $BD$ at point $F$. A line is drawn through point $D$ such that $DH\perp BC$ with $H$ as the foot of the perpendicular. $\triangle DCE$ is an isosceles triangle; if $\angle CDE=22.5^\circ$ and $DC=\sqrt{2}$, find the length of $GH$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:}\\
Since $\angle CDE=22.5^\circ$ and $CD=CE=\sqrt{2}$,\\
it follows that $\angle DCH=45^\circ$ and $DH\perp BC$,\\
thus $\angle HDC=\angle DCH=45^\circ$,\\
implying $DH=CH$,\\
since $DH^2+CH^2=DC^2=2$,\\
we have $DH=CH=1$,\\
since $\angle ABC=\angle DCH=45^\circ$,\\
$\triangle ABC$ is an isosceles right triangle.\\
Furthermore, since point G is the midpoint of BC,\\
$AG\perp BC$ and $AG=GC=BG$,\\
and since $BD=DE$ and $DH\perp BC$,\\
it follows $BH=HE=\sqrt{2}+1$,\\
since $BH=BG+GH=CG+GH=CH+GH+GH=\sqrt{2}+1$,\\
thus $1+2GH=\sqrt{2}+1$,\\
yielding $GH=\boxed{\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the bottom side is a horizontal straight line, and the order of the points from left to right is B, G, H, C, E; E is on the right side of C, that is, on the extension of BC. A is above G, D is above H and is located on AC; BD and AG intersect at F; DH is perpendicular to the bottom side and falls on H; DE connects from D obliquely downward to the right to E. In the figure, no clear equal-side-length marks are seen that directly indicate which two sides of △DCE are equal, but from the positions, ray CD points from C to the upper left, and ray CE points from C to the right, so ∠DCE is an obtuse angle. Then reason: The problem gives that △DCE is an isosceles triangle and ∠CDE=22.5°. First determine the equal sides: if CE=DE, then the base angles ∠DCE=∠CDE=22.5°, which would make ∠DCE an acute angle; if CD=DE, then ∠DCE=∠DEC=(180°−22.5°)/2=78.75°, also an acute angle. Both do not match the fact that ∠DCE in the figure is an obtuse angle. Therefore the isosceles relation can only be CD=CE. Thus CD=CE=√2, and ∠DEC=∠CDE=22.5°, so ∠DCE=180°−22.5°−22.5°=135°. Since CE and CH are on the same straight line and in opposite directions, ∠DCH=180°−135°=45°. Also DH⊥BC, and H, C are on BC, therefore △DHC is a right triangle; ∠DCH=45°, so △DHC is a 45°-45°-90° triangle. DC=√2 is the hypotenuse, hence DH=CH=1. Because D is on AC, and C, H, B are collinear, ∠ACB=∠DCH=45°. Also AB=AC, so the base angles of △ABC are equal, ∠ABC=45°, and thus △ABC is an isosceles right triangle. G is the midpoint of BC, therefore BG=GC. From BD=DE, and △DBH and △DEH are both right triangles with H as the right-angle vertex, and they share the right side DH, with hypotenuse BD=DE, so the two right triangles are congruent, obtaining BH=HE. Also H, C, E are collinear in order, and HC=1, CE=√2, so HE=HC+CE=1+√2, therefore BH=1+√2. From the order of B, G, H, C, BH=BG+GH. Also BG=GC, while GC=GH+CH=GH+1, so BH=(GH+1)+GH=1+2GH. Thus 1+2GH=1+√2, solving gives GH=√2/2.

raw_record.final_cot:
First describe the image: In the figure, the bottom side is a horizontal straight line, and the order of the points from left to right is B, G, H, C, E; E is on the right side of C, that is, on the extension of BC. A is above G, D is above H and is located on AC; BD and AG intersect at F; DH is perpendicular to the bottom side and falls on H; DE connects from D obliquely downward to the right to E. In the figure, no clear equal-side-length marks are seen that directly indicate which two sides of △DCE are equal, but from the positions, ray CD points from C to the upper left, and ray CE points from C to the right, so ∠DCE is an obtuse angle.

Then reason: The problem gives that △DCE is an isosceles triangle and ∠CDE=22.5°. First determine the equal sides: if CE=DE, then the base angles ∠DCE=∠CDE=22.5°, which would make ∠DCE an acute angle; if CD=DE, then ∠DCE=∠DEC=(180°−22.5°)/2=78.75°, also an acute angle. Both do not match the fact that ∠DCE in the figure is an obtuse angle. Therefore the isosceles relation can only be CD=CE.

Thus CD=CE=√2, and ∠DEC=∠CDE=22.5°, so ∠DCE=180°−22.5°−22.5°=135°. Since CE and CH are on the same straight line and in opposite directions, ∠DCH=180°−135°=45°.

Also DH⊥BC, and H, C are on BC, therefore △DHC is a right triangle; ∠DCH=45°, so △DHC is a 45°-45°-90° triangle. DC=√2 is the hypotenuse, hence DH=CH=1.

Because D is on AC, and C, H, B are collinear, ∠ACB=∠DCH=45°. Also AB=AC, so the base angles of △ABC are equal, ∠ABC=45°, and thus △ABC is an isosceles right triangle. G is the midpoint of BC, therefore BG=GC.

From BD=DE, and △DBH and △DEH are both right triangles with H as the right-angle vertex, and they share the right side DH, with hypotenuse BD=DE, so the two right triangles are congruent, obtaining BH=HE.

Also H, C, E are collinear in order, and HC=1, CE=√2, so HE=HC+CE=1+√2, therefore BH=1+√2.

From the order of B, G, H, C, BH=BG+GH. Also BG=GC, while GC=GH+CH=GH+1, so BH=(GH+1)+GH=1+2GH. Thus 1+2GH=1+√2, solving gives GH=√2/2.
